newsitem.title: CHINA: China to allow more banks in yuan business in '97.
newsitem.headline: China to allow more banks in yuan business in '97.

text.p: China will allow more foreign banks to conduct business in the local currency this year, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.
The newspaper quoted an official of the People's Bank of China, the central bank, as saying that applications by other banks were being reviewed and licences would be issued this year.
The newspaper, published by the official China Daily, gave no indication of the number of licences to be issued or the timing.

China recently announced its initial approval to allow lending and deposit-taking in yuan, the local currency, by four foreign banks with branches in Shanghai's Pudong district. The banks are Citicorp's Citibank subsidiary, HSBC Corp's Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp unit, the Industrial Bank of Japan and the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd.
Customers of the banks for local currency business will be confined to foreign-funded companies.
Except for these four banks, foreign financial institutions are restricted to taking deposits and making loans in foreign currency.
